title: Gordon Ramsay Is Blown Away By Tribe's Curry | Gordon's Great Escape
description: Gordon helps prepare a Nagaland curry and is blown away by the results.   #GordonRamsay #Cooking   Gordon Ramsay's Ultimate Cookery Course – http://amzn.to/2BzAud5 Subscribe for weekly cooking videos.   If you liked this clip check out the rest of Gordon's channels:  http://www.youtube.com/gordonramsay http://www.youtube.com/kitchennightmares http://www.youtube.com/thefword

asr.full_text: Now for the real reason I'm here, I'm going to see what makes a Nagaland curry so different to anything I've ever tasted before As I've been gifted the venison mr.. Honley is going to create a curry using the ball that he slaughtered So in the kidney kidney Hush kidney Liver and Belly and you cook everything same time? See, normally, we'd cook this separately. It's very rustic. Nothing's filleted, nothing's ever off the bone. And what's that dad's put in there? My father is putting another kind of leaf, which we find in the forest. And what's it like? It's quite citrus-y now. It's like lavender. We use even the fruits for like pepper Everything mr. Holly is using an eastish comes from his own land. This is the first Indian curry. I've seen made without any dried spices What's that the other chili? He's roasting it we have a better flavoring a fee rosette on the ash like that Yeah, it gives a better sense. Yeah, we got we do the same with peppers and The most surprising ingredient is something I've never seen before. It's bamboo shoot. Yeah, that's a fascinating smell, you know that. Slightly spicy edge to it. While the pork in the bamboo curry cooks, I'm going to try out these Nargilearn ingredients with my saddle of penicilln to see what I can come up with. BARRY RENOCHERNANI PEREIRA, PURSE CLUB OF BROW PENIS Pure fillet. Just a little touch. They intrigued me with the flavor there, you know that? Yeah. How do you turn up the gas? Thank you. How many Westerners have come cooking in this kitchen? None. No. I'm the first. Huh? Mm, it's a tradition in Scotland. We always have a swig each. Oh, yes. It means our passion is joined with a dish. While my venison curry reduces, Mr. Honley's pork and bamboo curry is already done, and I can't wait to taste it. The pork is delicious. Very tasty, the chili, the garlic... and the pork looks quite sort of boring and greasy... but flavour-wise delicious. That's delicious, the pork. The villagers from today's hunt that didn't get a cut of the deer, came to share mine. Very nice. Happy? Yes. Jordan? Yep? Just give them a second happen? Of course. There's real community spirit here and it makes eating together all that more enjoyable. Goodbye father, goodbye sister. If I don't see your endless board. The pork dish I tasted of theirs was amazing. You'd think that there was fifteen different spices. The dried bamboo, in terms of flavor is intense. Yeah it has an intriguing sort of turnip, stroke cardamon sort of slightly spicy edge to it. Who would ever believe we're in India? No spice! It's quite interesting, you dive into their world and you get rid of that monkey on your back and all of a sudden you start to relax in a big way and forget anything outside this village. I came in search of India's best keptkept culinary secrets, and Nagaland didn't disappoint. I've had my first taste of this region's indigenous ingredients, and I can't wait to see what other surprises the North East has in store. Thank you very much. Take care. Thank you. Made me feel so special. Best wishes. Thank you, Madawi. Take care. Upwards and onwards. And I've taken a bit of Nagaland with me. I want to use the bamboo shoot on my food store when I get back to Calcutta. Extraordinary, different, and incredibly rustic. Very humble, very simple, but fascinating food, though. Totally unspoiled. And in a way, nothing Indian.
